candidates.summary: Empty can answer from the index of the buffer's last non-blank token, found once, instead of a position-keyed cache whose lower-bound rescan no caller reaches
candidates.failure_scenario: No rendered page changes. The cached [blankFrom, blankTo) needs two bounds, a rescan branch and the 'Expr is never written' comment to stay right, and its `b.idx < b.blankFrom` half is reached by no caller: the only backward moves are Unget at commands.go:348 (after a GetNextN that started past the last Empty), readLength's restores at commands.go:438 and 449 (no Empty in between) and each method's restore to its own start; groups_test.go:108 calls Empty only at idx == len. Empty is true exactly when idx is past the last token that is not a space or a comment, so one lazily computed `last` (scan back from the end over the trailing run, once per buffer) answers every call with `if b.idx > b.last { b.idx = max(b.idx, len(b.Expr)); return true }; return false`, nothing to invalidate whatever order the position moves in, and the same linear cost.
candidates.verify_by: Replace blankFrom/blankTo with a lazily set `last int` (plus a computed flag) as above, run `go test -count=1 ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/markdown/mathml/` and time ConvertDisplay on 65,536 indented `%` lines against the branch: expect green and the same time
